newsitem.title: UK: India's SBI sets automation programme.
newsitem.headline: India's SBI sets automation programme.

text.p: State Bank of India, the country's largest bank, aims to automate 2,000 of its branches by March 1999, chairman P Kakodlar told bankers in London.
"We plan a 3.79 billion rupee investment over the next few years and this money comes from an established deposit and which is sheltered from tax," he said.
The bank, which has over 8,800 branches in India is aiming to raise up to $400 million from overseas investors via an issue of global depositary receipts (GDRs).
As a result of the issue, the Reserve Bank of India's stake will fall from 66.3 percent to 59.6-60 percent, Kakodlar said.

He said that the bank is not aiming to reduce its rural network because although some of the branches were not profitable, they provided a steady deposit base on which the bank can build its corporate and high-marging lending.
"Fifty-five percent of deposits come from individuals, which means our deposit base is fundamentally stable," Kakodlar said.
